ARAMRAM, JAMES'S DELIGHT (20/1) — exposed, 17th here last year (James's Delight). THE GROUND IS THE RACE: soft, heavy in places, at Haydock 6f — a stamina test; proven soft form: Marvelman (G2 win on soft, G1 3rd on GS); Almeraq (GS handicap only); Paborus (8th on GS); Kind Of Blue, Big Mojo, Coppull unknown. THE BLANCO LINE (within 4lb of the top 119): Almeraq 119 (USED), Kind Of Blue 118 (READ — the placer, unproven ground), Marvelman 117 (USED — the pick), Big Mojo 117 (USED — the second danger), all read, none passed on a number. THE BOOKMAKER'S QUESTION: why three at 3/1-7/2? Because the top-rated horse flopped last time, the second is a placer, and the third is a 7f horse — the market cannot separate class, consistency and ground; the ground is the fact the market has priced least. THE DOWN-TO-TWO TEST: Marvelman (proven on the ground, fresh, 3rd in a G1 two weeks ago) v Almeraq (the best horse on the figures, on ground he has never raced on at this level, after a flop). The Haydock 1:55 lesson (the tell) — Haggas/Marquand is a top yard and the number one, but not Godolphin's big-day tell; the Ascot lesson — read the race's DNA: last year the 16/1 shot beat the placer and the favourite lost; the DNA says this race is not won by the obvious one. PACE: Marvelman leads or presses (made the running at York); Big Mojo 'up with the pace'; Coppull handy; Almeraq and Kind Of Blue held up. On soft, the leader who stays wins — Marvelman's shape. BET SHAPE: 8 runners, three at 3/1-7/2, concentration low — WIN at 7/2 (3 places at 1/5 are worth little at this price). VERDICT: MARVELMAN, WIN, 7/2 (4.5; 5.2 exchange). NAMED DANGER: Almeraq — if class carries on soft, he is the best horse. SECOND DANGER: Big Mojo — course, distance, the race's own winner, back in form, Buick. What would make me wrong: Almeraq handling the ground (his Ayr GS win says he might); or Coppull's ceiling. GRADE: B — the ground line is a fact, the pace line is a read, the class question is honest.
